I don't know if you are just a fanboy that is incapable of looking at it objectively but VR and 4K are not at all comparable.

4K is a straight upgrade to existing game development that is still compatible with old hardware.

VR is an entirely new interface that requires games not only to be customized for it but also requires developers to rethink how a game should be played and controlled to maximize the experience.

If I'm a developer I can make my new game in 4K at minimal incremental added cost and rest assured that even if the 4K player base is small I won't lose sales because people can still play it at lower resolutions. 4K also has the benefit of allowing me to make higher quality promotional material I can use for marketing.

If I'm a developer and I'm thinking about making a VR game I have to accept far more risk because it is an entirely new way of designing games and I would have to spend resources trying to figure out what works best and at the end of the day I can only sell the game to the small pool of people that have bought into VR.

I'm not arguing that VR won't catch on but to suggest that it already has become popular is just being blind to reality and I think if you asked any VR developer they would agree.
